it’s not possible to ascertain which trait was selected-for and which trait was the free-rider

This is pretty fucking retarded. If I have a batch of drosphila flies, and I select specifically for the white mutant trait, and exclude the other flies from the gene pool, I know for a fact what is the trait that has been selected for. Even from a scientific perspective of looking at animals in the wild, it is empirically possible to demonstrate with high certainty what traits are being selected for.

(1) the claim that evolution is a process in which creatures with adaptive traits are selected (2) the claim that evolution is a process in which creatures are selected for their adaptive traits

This has to be an intentionally bad framing of the definition of adaptation. 2 does not follow 1 because creatures are not being "selected for adaptive traits." A heritable trait's positive effect on selection makes it adaptive, not vice versa. Nobody infers that "creatures are selected for their adaptive traits", because having been selected is what makes it adaptive in the first place. The word for implies that there is an intention, and quite simply, there is not. Only an outcome.

Evolution argues that there are heritable traits which may increase the likelihood of sexual selection in a species. Evolution is not "selecting for adaptive traits." Among the population of a species, there are those with traits that can be seen to have increased the likelihood of sexual reproduction in a particular environment. Among those traits there are heritable ones. A heritable trait which has increased the likelihood of sexual reproduction is then, by definition adaptive.
